what_its_for: Famotidine is used to treat and prevent heartburn, acid indigestion, and sour stomach. It is also used to treat ulcers in the stomach and small intestine, and a condition called GERD (gastroesophageal reflux disease), where stomach acid backs up into the esophagus. It works by reducing the amount of acid your stomach makes.
how_to_take: Take famotidine exactly as directed on the package or as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. If you are using it to prevent heartburn, take it 15 to 60 minutes before eating a meal or drinking a beverage that may cause heartburn. If you are taking the chewable tablet, chew it completely before swallowing. Do not take more than directed.
dosing: For over-the-counter heartburn relief in adults and children 12 years and older: the usual dose is 10 mg to 20 mg taken once or twice daily. Do not take more than 40 mg in 24 hours unless your doctor tells you to. For prescription doses, follow your doctor's specific instructions, as the dose may be higher for treating ulcers or GERD. Always read the label carefully and do not exceed the recommended dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store famotidine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other antacids or acid-reducing medicines at the same time unless your doctor approves. Try to avoid foods and drinks that trigger your heartburn, such as spicy foods, fatty foods, chocolate, coffee, alcohol, and carbonated drinks. Avoid smoking, as it can increase stomach acid. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before combining famotidine with other medications, including prescription drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: trouble swallowing or painful swallowing, vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds, bloody or black tarry stools, chest pain or severe stomach pain, unexplained weight loss, heartburn that has not improved after 14 days of use, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing, or if you feel confused or unusually tired.
when_it_works: Famotidine typically starts to relieve heartburn symptoms within 15 to 60 minutes after taking it. The effects can last for up to 10 to 12 hours. For treating ulcers or GERD with prescription doses, it may take several days to a few weeks before you notice full improvement. Continue taking it as directed even if you start to feel better.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): You may be more sensitive to the effects of famotidine. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease, tell your doctor before taking famotidine, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using famotidine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as they will help weigh the benefits and risks for you and your baby. Children under 12 years: Do not give over-the-counter famotidine to children under 12 years of age unless directed by a doctor.
